data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failure than a large redundant service because it disrupts 'monoculture-driven' common mode failures through heterogeneous operational environments.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The decentralized services all rely on a single shared dependency (e.g., a common cloud provider's DNS or a ubiquitous library like OpenSSL as suggested in SCR_003).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The cost of coordination in the decentralized network leads to a systemic consensus collapse (SCR_002).","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Heterogeneity in deployment (different OS, kernels, hardware, and configurations) across independent operators prevents a single exploit or bug from triggering a global outage, whereas a large service\u2014despite internal redundancy\u2014typically employs a standardized 'golden image' or unified CI/CD pipeline that propagates failures instantly to all redundant nodes.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
